headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Roo Code can modify shared workspace state while slim can write container artifacts, creating dangerous cross-agent interference and leakage paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code ingests workspace files and can use MCP, while slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts in a temporary container. If slim writes attacker-controlled content into a shared workspace or mounted artifact path, Roo Code may treat it as trusted input. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so interaction risk is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace or mounted directory
IF slim writes content that Roo Code later reads as instructions or configuration
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Mount shared paths read-only for Roo Code
Disable MCP on Roo Code for untrusted content
Add a manual review step before Roo Code consumes slim outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; slim touches container images, environment variables, and certificate private keys. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so a shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive material across the pair. No isolation or redaction is documented.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets, keys, or sensitive build artifacts in a shared directory
IF outputs from one agent are forwarded to the other without redaction
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Use separate credentials per agent
Redact private keys and env vars before handoff
Restrict outbound network for the agent handling secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shells; Roo Code also modifies git state, while slim operates on container images and artifacts. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git state, and neither profile shows locking or coordination. This is a default-dangerous overlap.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF Roo Code and slim run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write operations
Disable git writes for one agent during shared runs
Use a lock file or orchestrator mutex

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code or instructions from workspace context, and slim can emit container-analysis outputs from stdin/stdout. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect builds or container changes. The pair has no documented validation boundary, but slim is not inherently an action-taking agent.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes slim output as authoritative input
IF the orchestrator forwards analysis results into shell commands or build steps without validation
mitigations: Insert a human review gate
Validate outputs against schemas
Require explicit confirmation before shell execution
Log and diff all handoffs between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while slim handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, and environment variables. If these data classes are processed under different residency or retention regimes, the pair can create a compliance breach. Only profile fields are cited because the risk is driven by each agent’s own data handling, not a shared documented channel.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal data are placed into either agent’s workspace
IF the deployment applies different retention or residency rules to model prompts versus container artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Use separate retention policies per workspace
Mask secrets before analysis
Document residency and deletion handling
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls
